papers.title_en: One Future, Every Robot: Label-Efficient Collective-State Prediction with Decentralized JEPA
papers.authors: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Garvilov, Sergey Muravyov
papers.evidence: 去中心化JEPA让每个机器人从局部观察和受限消息预测共同的未来集体状态
papers.tldr: 针对机器人集群仅凭局部观测与有限带宽消息预测共同未来状态的问题，提出CS-JEPA，一种无需全局池化与目标编码器的循环联合嵌入预测架构。部署时各机器人使用16帧历史与每条有向边64维消息，经预训练后冻结表示仅用极少全局标注即可适应拓扑与规模变化。实验表明其预测误差与机器人间一致性标签预算AUC在多达108机器人场景全面优于基线，并在分支价值预测上显著提升。
papers.abstract_en: Can every robot in a swarm predict the same future collective state from only local observations and bandwidth-limited messages? We formulate this as decentralized shared-state prediction and introduce Collective-State JEPA (CS-JEPA), a recurrent joint-embedding predictive architecture whose output at every robot represents one common future token field. At deployment, each robot uses a 16-frame local history and one 64-float recurrent message per directed edge; there is no global pooling, target encoder, episode clock, or recorded future action. After pretraining without downstream collective labels, frozen representations are evaluated with ridge probes fitted on 6, 12, or 24 globally labeled episodes. Against raw-future reconstruction with the same receiver anchor and deployment capacity but 9,607 additional training-only parameters, a prospectively registered five-seed follow-up improves prediction-error and inter-robot-agreement label-budget AUC on in-distribution, ring, mutual-kNN, and unseen-size families up to 108 robots. Every effect favors CS-JEPA in 5/5 outer seeds. In a separate sealed eight-seed follow-up, matched action-conditioned predictors receive each candidate four-step plan before producing receiver-local predictive representations. CS-JEPA reduces branch-value MSE by 45.5% and improves within-context candidate-score Pearson correlation by 0.1291, with both effects favorable in 8/8 seeds, including at unseen N=32. These results support common-future JEPA targets as a label-efficient primitive for decentralized swarm prediction under topology and size shift, with additional evidence of planning-relevant value estimation.

papers.title_en: LeapBot-WA: World-Anchor Action Models via Predictive Latent Alignments
papers.authors: Pei Liu, Nan Zheng, Lang Zhang, Daojie Peng, Yanan Zhang, Feilong Kong, Mingyue Feng, Jiachao Liu, Yaonong Wang, Qifeng Chen, Jun Ma
papers.evidence: 基于预测性潜在对齐的世界锚定动作模型，可迁移至多机器人环境表示
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型（WAMs）依赖像素级视频生成，导致计算瓶颈且易受视觉干扰。本文提出LeapBot-WA，将联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）作为世界锚点，建立预测潜在对齐范式，在潜在基础空间中提取抽象物理动态，取代视觉合成。为解决非高斯预测特征与扩散先验的模态差距，引入各向同性语义自编码器（ISAE），重塑锚点潜空间为扩散友好流形。设计非对称混合Transformer（MoT），训练时锚点扩散Transformer指导动作扩散Transformer，推理时剪除重分支实现零开销。在LIBERO上达预测模型最优，媲美顶级生成式WAM于RoboTwin 2.0，且无需大规模轨迹预训练，展现强零样本鲁棒性与真实世界迁移能力，为可扩展机器人控制提供高效鲁棒的潜在中心范式。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for embodied intelligence, yet the prevailing reliance on pixel-level video generation creates a fundamental bottleneck. Forcing models to reconstruct task-irrelevant visual details dissipates representational capacity and renders policies vulnerable to visual distractors. In this paper, we propose LeapBot-WA, which establishes a novel Predictive-Latent paradigm for WAMs by operationalizing the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) as a World-Anchor. Departing from the traditional reliance on visual synthesis, LeapBot-WA shifts the core of world modeling to Predictive Semantic Alignment, extracting abstract physical dynamics directly within a latent foundation space. To bridge the modality gap between non-Gaussian predictive features and diffusion priors, we introduce the Isotropic Semantic Autoencoder (ISAE), which reshapes the anchor's latent space into a diffusion-friendly manifold to prevent off-manifold drift. Furthermore, we design an Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. During training, an Anchor Diffusion Transformer acts as a privileged dynamics expert to guide the Action Diffusion Transformer; at inference, this heavy dynamics branch is pruned, enabling zero-overhead execution. LeapBot-WA achieves state-of-the-art performance among predictive models on LIBERO and matches top-tier generative WAMs on RoboTwin 2.0 without requiring large-scale trajectory pre-training. It further demonstrates superior zero-shot robustness to unseen environments and successful real-world transfer, establishing a highly efficient and robust latent-centric paradigm for scalable robotic control. Code: https://github.com/LeapWM/leapbot-wa.

papers.title_en: MARS-RA: Rank Aggregation for Credit Assignment via Multimodal Comparisons in Embodied Multi-Agent Cooperation
papers.authors: Dawei Wang, Di Zhao, Xinyuan Liu, Marci Chi Ma, Xiaoyang Liu, Chengming Zhou, Gary Ushaw, Richard Davison
papers.evidence: 面向具身多智能体协作的基于多模态比较的信用分配
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习中的信用分配在具身AI场景下面临反馈稀疏且延迟、活跃智能体数量动态变化等挑战。MARS-RA将信用分配重构为排名聚合问题，利用大多模态模型对智能体贡献进行成对比较，转而采用相对估计而非绝对估计，从而对噪声和动态参与具有鲁棒性。聚合得到的贡献分数用于势能型奖励塑形，并提供收敛性与鲁棒性理论保证，Shapley值可作为解释参考。实验表明该方法能在多种困难任务中有效指导智能体协同合作。
papers.abstract_en: Credit assignment is a fundamental challenge in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, particularly in embodied AI settings characterized by limited and delayed feedback as well as dynamically changing numbers of active agents. We propose MARS-RA, a framework that reformulates credit assignment as a rank aggregation problem using contribution-based pairwise comparisons among agents generated by large multimodal models. This shift from absolute to relative estimation ensures robustness against noise and dynamic agent participation, converting comparison results into contribution scores for potential-based reward shaping. We provide theoretical justification for the convergence and robustness of the proposed framework, and show that Shapley values can be used as an interpretive reference. Experimental results on challenging tasks of different types indicate that MARS-RA can guide agents toward effective cooperation.

papers.title_en: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Gain Tuning in Control of Teleoperation Manipulators with Joint Flexibility and Time-Varying Delays
papers.authors: Armin Attarzadeh, Mohammad Ali Ghaemifar, Alireza Khanzadeh, Soheil Ganjefar
papers.evidence: 结合P+d控制器与TD3强化学习的混合控制，保证主从遥操作机器人在时延下的稳定协调
papers.tldr: 针对含关节柔性的双边遥操作系统，时变网络延迟常导致系统失稳与主从跟踪误差增大。本文设计一种混合控制策略，以P+d控制器保障基础稳定性，并引入TD3深度强化学习智能体实时调节从端比例和阻尼增益，从而抑制柔性振动、提高跟踪精度。通过Lyapunov-Krasovskii理论证明了有界时变延迟下的稳定性，实验结果验证了该方法在关节柔性和不确定延迟同时存在时的有效性与实用性，为遥操作控制提供新型自适应增益调节方案。
papers.abstract_en: Bilateral teleoperation systems that include joint flexibility better reflect real robotic systems used in surgery, space, and rehabilitation. However, joint flexibility together with time-varying communication delays makes it difficult to maintain stable and coordinated motion between the master and slave robots. To address this, we propose a hybrid control method that combines a stable Proportional-plus-Damping (P+d) controller with a model-free deep reinforcement learning agent based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. The P+d controller provides basic stability under bounded delays, while the learning agent adjusts and tunes the remote-side proportional and damping gains in real time to reduce vibrations and improve tracking. Stability is guaranteed for bounded time-varying delays using Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis. The approach provides a practical solution for teleoperation systems facing both joint flexibility and uncertain network delays.

papers.title_en: NeurGO: Learning to Generate Elite Candidates for Meta-Black-Box Expensive Optimization
papers.authors: Jintao He, Huixiang Zhen, Wenyin Gong
papers.evidence: 面向昂贵黑箱优化的生成式MetaBBO框架，可用于多机器人系统中的进化优化
papers.tldr: 昂贵黑箱优化在科学与工程中广泛存在，传统演化算法与元黑箱优化常将多数评估耗于候选筛选，浪费预算；代理模型辅助方法又受限于有限数据与模型偏差。为此提出NeurGO，一种生成式MetaBBO框架，用注意力编码器捕捉种群搜索趋势，解码器直接合成精英候选，并以质量-多样性损失维持种群多样性。在CEC 2008与COCO BBOB上，同等评估预算下优化性能更优且收敛更快。
papers.abstract_en: Expensive black-box optimization is ubiquitous in science and engineering, where function evaluations are costly and the evaluation budget is limited. Traditional evolutionary algorithms and Meta-BlackBox Optimization (MetaBBO) approaches typically consume most evaluations on candidate selection, often wasting precious budget on inferior solutions. Although surrogate-assisted evolution and Bayesian optimization aim to reduce evaluations through surrogate models, constructing an accurate global model from limited data remains challenging, and model bias can easily trap the search in local optima. To overcome these limitations, we propose NeurGO, a generative MetaBBO framework that directly synthesizes elite candidates from historical population states. Specifically, we employ an attention-based encoder to capture the population-level search trend and condition a decoder on this representation to generate high-quality candidates, avoiding the expensive evaluation of large offspring pools. We then design a quality-diversity loss to maintain solution quality and population diversity throughout the search. Through extensive benchmarking on CEC 2008 and the COCO BBOB test suites, our method achieves better optimization performance under the same evaluation budget and exhibits faster convergence.

papers.title_en: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.evidence: 基于动作条件世界模型的通用机器人规划与环境表征
papers.tldr: 模仿学习策略在特定训练环境中表现良好，但泛化能力不足，难以适应新场景和任务。为此提出世界动作规划器，融合视觉语言模型的推理能力与多任务姿态图像条件世界模型的物理基础，利用想象的世界模型展开进行优化和搜索，迭代调整初始计划。在组合任务、新布局及零样本泛化上显著超越VLA等端到端策略模型，为通用机器人决策提供了一种有效可行途径。
papers.abstract_en: Building generalizable agents for diverse applications remains a fundamental challenge. While imitation learning-based policies succeed in specific training environments, they often fail to generalize to novel scenes and tasks. In this work, we propose World Action Planner, a robot planning system that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and the physical grounding of a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model. Our system enables an agent to propose initial action plans and iteratively refine them via optimization and search, reasoning over imagined world model rollouts. We demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot generalization scenarios, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art end-to-end policy models such as VLAs and WAMs. Project website at worldactionplanner.github.io
